record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not

claims.claim: Multiple transferable L1 records report absolute oral bioavailability well below 20% for large peptidomimetic/macrocyclic drugs: olcegepant %F<1, quinupristin/dalfopristin <5%, docetaxel 8%, UK-427,857 2.9%, almorexant ~11%, methysergide 13%, and YH4808 10.1%.

The query is a large, highly polar, fully ionized macrocyclic peptidomimetic, and the most structurally relevant transferable low-F contexts are also large peptidomimetic/macrocyclic agents, supporting transfer of their low-F outcomes.
Retosiban is the only borderline record (17-25%) and does not affirmatively establish F>=20%; it also notes extensive first-pass elimination.
Cadazolid's very low F, inferred from high CL/F and V/F, is consistent with the low-F direction.

evidence_gaps: No direct absolute oral bioavailability measurement for the query molecule itself is supplied.
No matched oral versus IV exposure data for the query are available; transfer relies on structurally related contexts.
Retosiban's borderline 17-25% range leaves some threshold ambiguity, but it is not used as positive evidence.
No formulation or food-effect data are provided; solubility/dissolution is mixed or unclear.
